children: The content_edges store — from_id/to_id binary_id foreign keys whose FK constraint makes a Dangling Reference physically unstorable.
Content Edges Table (content_edges, Migration 20260614230000) is the materialized backbone of the Content Graph. Each row is a directed edge: from_id and to_id are binary_id columns, both
onto the documents table. The Edge Projector writes rows here from the edges emitted by each plugin's Edge Extractor.
Because to_id is an FK, you

insert an edge whose target does not exist. There is no dangling column and no soft target — a missing target is rejected by Postgres at write time. This is deliberate: the table only ever holds real, resolvable edges, so Graph Traversal never has to defend against broken rows.
The consequence is that a Dangling Reference — a Reference Field pointing at a deleted or unpublished Document — is never persisted. Instead it is computed at
and surfaced as a Phantom Node. The table stays clean; the dangling-ness lives only in the query layer.
Blast Radius runs a reverse-reference lookup (to_id = ?) before delete/unpublish.
Graph Traversal BFS-walks from_id/to_id from a root Document.
An Orphan Node is simply a document that appears in neither column.
All three are served headlessly under /v1/graph on the HTTP API v1. This mirrors how the Indx Engine keeps its search index as the single materialized read surface.
